```motoi
(define (bump x) (set! x (+ x 1)) x)
(define n 0)
(bump n)   ; => 1
n          ; => 0, why?
```
`set!` on a parameter mutates the local binding. `n` outside is untouched.
how do I actually update n

Reassign the returned value:

```motoi
(set! n (bump n))
```
or use a closure over n
Or box it. Or make `bump` explicitly mutate a shared reference. Depends on the shape you want.
Cleaner. Encapsulates state, doesn't leak into the caller's scope.
Scheme passes by value at the reference level. Parameter mutation stays local.

`=` for numbers. `eq?` for identity (same object). `equal?` for structural equality.

Always `=` for numbers. `eq?` on numbers is unreliable across implementations.

processing a 100k-item list with (define (walk lst) (cons (f (car lst)) (walk (cdr lst)))) — stack overflow
Non-tail. Every `cons` wraps the recursive call.

Accumulator + reverse at the end:

```motoi
(define (walk lst)
  (let loop ((lst lst) (acc '()))
    (if (null? lst) (reverse acc)
        (loop (cdr lst) (cons (f (car lst)) acc)))))
```
Yes — O(n), single pass. Cheaper than a stack overflow.
If you don't need incremental — `(map f lst)` does exactly this, tail-safe in most Schemes.

Two paddles, a ball. Start with the ball.

```motoi
(define ball-x 64) (define ball-y 64)
(define ball-dx 1) (define ball-dy 1)
```

```motoi
(set! ball-x (+ ball-x ball-dx))
(set! ball-y (+ ball-y ball-dy))
(when (or (<= ball-y 0) (>= ball-y 127)) (set! ball-dy (- ball-dy)))
```

```motoi
(when (and (<= ball-x 4) (<= left-y ball-y (+ left-y paddle-h)))
  (set! ball-dx (- ball-dx)))
(when (and (>= ball-x 124) (<= right-y ball-y (+ right-y paddle-h)))
  (set! ball-dx (- ball-dx)))
```

```motoi
(when (key? 'w) (set! left-y (max 0 (- left-y 2))))
(when (key? 's) (set! left-y (min (- 127 paddle-h) (+ left-y 2))))
(when (key? 'up)   (set! right-y (max 0 (- right-y 2))))
(when (key? 'down) (set! right-y (min (- 127 paddle-h) (+ right-y 2))))
```

```motoi
(define score-l 0) (define score-r 0)
(when (< ball-x 0) (set! score-r (+ score-r 1)) (reset-ball!))
(when (> ball-x 127) (set! score-l (+ score-l 1)) (reset-ball!))
```

